data.title: Deletion Sensitivity Is a Property of the Model: A Three-Condition Measurement over 72 Valid Experimental Cells
data.description: arXiv:2611.13223v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Reasoning models write a trace at every turn of a multi-turn tool session, and later turns read it. Upstream providers hold different retention constraints, so a request forwarded across issuers arrives with its history deleted, and its task cost remains unmeasured. This paper reports a direct, blind, multi-seed measurement of full history deletion in multi-turn tool calling, through three rendering conditions, a calibrated set of 72 valid experimental cells, a multi-seed protocol, and the official checker. The same deletion separates the models by direction and by magnitude, one class losing tens of points, another gaining, and a third unchanged, with the endpoint ordering reproduced across seeds and task subsets modulating the magnitude and, near zero, the sign. A re-dosed model preserves its success across the full deletion range, so the reading belongs to the model rather than the dose. Deletion sensitivity is a model-level property under an operational definition, measured under a fixed task family, scorer, and protocol, and a retrained model is a new model that a two-cell screen, one retention run and one deletion run, re-reads for the cost of two runs. Deletion sensitivity is thus a measurable property of the model, and the reading must enter routing as prior information rather than persist as an invisible default cost.
data.author: Yiran Li, Hanzhang Jia, Liheng Zeng, Zhiyu Yang, Yi Gao
